title: Trade and comparative advantage
scope: Read complete manuscript, all five worked examples, all eight prompts/solutions, teach-back and retention, full benchmark/inputs/README/checker, six proposed source scopes and full author review. No manuscript/shared files changed.
mathematical_review: Ricardian choice is a global linear production optimum with equality-price correspondences. Both original and Exercise1 equilibrium clear labor, ownership income, consumer budgets, goods and balanced bilateral payments. The complete-specialization candidate p=2 fails Exercise1; the actual p=1 endpoint lets Foreign diversify. Weak gains proof does not claim universal strict or individual gains.

Fixed-coefficient factor equations are restricted to the strict diversification cone and positive supporting rewards. The primal-dual bound is correct and global. Comparative statics and purchasing power in both goods have the displayed signs. Outside-cone Exercise2 uses the correct feasible unique corner and zero wage on unused labor.

Compensation uses actual lump-sum income transfer and common prices, rather than treating a representative utility gain as automatic redistribution. Exact squared utility gains and independent high-precision interval confirm that transfer15 strictly benefits both ownership groups.

Conditional destination choice covers zero exports, the strictly concave positive-price interval and the dominated zero-price tail. Negative margins are excluded before squaring; positive setup cost makes the cutoff numerator condition necessary. Exact indifference retains both choices. Sunk80 versus avoidable80 changes shutdown profit, not the operating first-order condition.

Scale and selection are explicitly distinguished from a causal learning effect and from a full general-equilibrium industry result. Delivered versus produced quantities and real setup costs have consistent units. Changes in residual demand can overturn a held-fixed trade-cost comparison.

Small and large tariff models use supported quasilinear surplus measures, domestic ownership and one count of revenue. Complementarity and no-trade plateaus replace invalid extrapolated negative imports. Foreign offer price is distinguished from a nonexistent border transaction.

Large-country national objective is strictly concave over positive trade, and the whole no-trade plateau is compared with the interior optimum. Foreign cost and welfare are explicitly supplied; the terms-of-trade gain is a transfer, not a world resource gain. Retaliation and other response changes invalidate the stated unilateral optimum.

Shipping Exercise8 replaces a fiscal transfer with real numeraire consumption. Identical observed price wedges and quantities therefore coexist with different welfare accounts. Recipient/input evidence is correctly required before attributing the wedge.
